messages:
elaine: Weekly acct health check — AcmeCorp showing a spike in error rate this morning. Can eng/sre share a quick 24h breakdown (5xx, timeouts, 429) + top failing endpoints? cc @vikram @toni

vikram: On it, pulling analytics now. will post numbers in ~1m.

deploy-bot: deploy notice: service-inference v2.7.3 deployed to prod at 2026-02-28T09:14:02Z by ci/cd (canary=enabled)

vikram: Raw 24h summary from analytics: total requests 1,200,430, total errors 28,400 (2.37%). Breakdown below:
```
5xx: 19,100 (1.59%) — mostly 503, 500 at peak window 09:10-09:25 UTC
Timeouts (504/client side): 6,200 (0.52%) — correlated with longer tails
Rate limits (429): 1,100 (0.09%) — short bursts from a few orgs
```
Top failing endpoints (by error count):
```
/v1/generate          12,400 errors — predominately 503s
/v1/embeddings        7,800 errors  — mostly timeouts (batch jobs)
/v1/chat/stream       5,200 errors  — mix of 429s + timeouts
/v1/health              900 errors  — short burst during node restart
```
Numbers sum ~28.4k (matches above). 90th percentile of errors come from 3 orgs; AcmeCorp is the largest single contributor (~41% of error volume).

toni: SRE corroborates. Seeing two infra node restarts on shard-3 at 09:12 and 09:20 UTC, both followed by short flood of 503s. I/O queue depth spiked and kept connections waiting. Sample from logs: 
```
[09:14:06] inference-host-3 | ERROR | upstream response 503 service-unavailable
[09:14:07] inference-host-3 | WARN  | request timeout after 30s
```
Root cause looks like transient I/O saturation + heavier-than-expected onboarding traffic.

nina: That aligns with AcmeCorp onboarding batch — they ramped 3x at 09:00 (per onboarding notes). Renewal conversation scheduled EOM — this is a potential risk if we don't stabilize their experience. Also asked billing to hold off auto-invoice change until we confirm usage is valid.

vikram: Latency impact: baseline p50/p95 ~180ms/420ms. During spike p50/p95 jumped to ~260ms/980ms. Retries increased, bumping their token spend estimate +12% for the day.

elaine: Can we mitigate before EOD? Options: throttle their batch, rollback canary, add capacity, or temporary org-level rate-limit. What do you recommend?

toni: Immediate plan I can execute: 1) enable autoscale burst on shard-3 (if capacity available), 2) apply temp org-level soft-rate-limit for AcmeCorp (e.g., 60req/s -> 20req/s), 3) rollback to v2.7.2 canary for inference if we see the same kernel regressions. I'll open incident ticket and start with soft rate-limit now. I'll also watch metrics for 15m.

vikram: I'll prepare a route pin for AcmeCorp to model-small variant and disable streaming partials for their worklow; submit PR and can push rule in 10m.

nina: I'll notify AcmeCorp TAM + CSM to ask them to pause large batch jobs until we've stabilized. Also adding this to the renewal playbook as a risk note.

elaine: Perfect. Please update here when rate-limit or rollback happens. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: action: applied org-rate-limit AcmeCorp -> 20req/s at 09:38 UTC by ops-rule-engine

toni: Rate-limit applied. Observing error-rate drop in realtime. Starting autoscale burst now. If error-rate doesn't fall back under 0.5% in 10m, I'll do canary rollback.

vikram: PR merged to pin route -> model-small for AcmeCorp (temp). Disabling streaming partials for their org.

deploy-bot: rollback: inference v2.7.2 canary rolled out for AcmeCorp at 09:48 UTC, id=rb-1764528500

toni: Rollback completed. Current 24h error rate recalculated (rolling window): 1.24% (down from 2.37%). p95 latency back to ~430ms. Will leave autoscale and rate-limit for 2h then reassess.

nina: Noted — I'll update the customer + include a note in renewal materials. Thanks team.

elaine: Great work, team. Please add postmortem notes to the incident ticket and tag me. We'll re-check weekly if AcmeCorp ramps again. :raised_hands:
